```{r}
# z_value outliers
outlier_z_value <- data.frame()
# filter to a needed dependent variable
outlier_z_value <- appliances %>%
  filter(dep_variable_purchase_category %in% c("purschase (probability) of efficient appliance", "WTP for efficient appliance"))
# exclude the outliers
outlier_z_value <- outlier_z_value %>% 
                  filter(z_value < -0.5 |
                         z_value > 0.5)
# Anderson, Claxton (1982) - fridge - economic - revealed
# Schultz et al. (2015) - very specific intensive intervention - a marketing campaign - lighting - economic - revealed
# Train, Atherton (1995) x5 - confusing modelling - fridge, ac - information - stated
# Li et al. (2021) - fridge - economic - stated
# Skourtos et al. (2021) x4 - fridge - economic - stated
# Ward et al. (2021) x2 - fridge - economic - stated
```


```{r}
# data for > 1 intervention

data_purchase_multi <- appliances_multi %>% 
  filter(dep_variable_purchase_category %in% c("purschase (probability) of efficient appliance", "WTP for efficient appliance"))
# 40 obs
table(data_purchase_multi$multi_intervention)

# introduce variables intervention1 and intervention2 and implement a meta-regression
# this is actually intervention 2 technically as we are over-writing
data_purchase_multi$intervention1 <- with(data_purchase_multi, case_when(
  feedback == 1 ~ "Information",
  information == 1 ~ "Information",
  label == 1 ~ "Label",
  rebate == 1 ~ "Rebate",
  tax_credit == 1 ~ "Tax",
  subsidy == 1 ~ "Subsidy",
  loan == 1 ~ "Loan",
  choice_architecture == 1 ~ "Command & Control",
  TRUE ~ NA_character_
))

data_purchase_multi$intervention2 <- with(data_purchase_multi, case_when(
  (feedback == 1 & intervention1 != "Information") ~ "Information",
  (information == 1 & intervention1 != "Information") ~ "Information",
  (label == 1 & intervention1 != "Label") ~ "Label",
  (rebate == 1 & intervention1 != "Rebate") ~ "Rebate",
  (tax_credit == 1 &  intervention1 != "Tax") ~ "Tax",
  (subsidy == 1 & intervention1 != "Subsidy") ~ "Subsidy",
  (loan == 1 & intervention1 != "Loan") ~ "Loan",
  (choice_architecture == 1 &intervention1 != "Command & Control") ~ "Command & Control",
  TRUE ~ NA_character_
)) 

meta_model_multi <- rma(z_value, z_variance, data = data_purchase_multi, method = "FE", mods = ~ intervention1:intervention2+0)
summary(meta_model_multi)

meta_model_multi_reml <- rma(z_value, z_variance, data = data_purchase_multi, method = "REML", mods = ~ intervention1:intervention2+0)
summary(meta_model_multi_reml)
```

```{r}
### ANALYSIS BY APPLIANCE ###

                 seTE = z_variance,
```

```{r}
### META-ANALYSIS ###
### PURCHASE PROBABILITY + WTP (incl. outliers)

### FIXED EFFECTS ###
meta_model1 <- rma(z_value, z_variance, data = data_purchase3, method = "FE", mods = ~ intervention+0)
summary(meta_model1)
# fixed effects by intervention
# all significant positive

meta_model2 <- rma(z_value, z_variance, data = data_purchase3, method = "FE", mods = ~ appliance+0)
summary(meta_model2)
# fixed effects by appliance
# AC, light, fridge, tv, washing machine, water heater significant positive

### RANDOM EFFECTS ###
meta_model3 <- rma(z_value, z_variance, data = data_purchase3, method = "REML", mods = ~ intervention+0)
summary(meta_model3)
# random effects by intervention
# information, label, rebate significant positive
meta_model4 <- rma(z_value, z_variance, data = data_purchase3, method = "REML", mods = ~ appliance+0)
summary(meta_model4)
# random effects by appliance
# AC, light, fridge, washing machine, water heater significant positive

### MULTI-LEVEL MODEL ###

#Above results show that there is no statistical difference between effect sizes for 1) wtp and purchase prob 2)monetary incentives and info strategies

meta_model5 <-rma.mv(z_value, z_variance, mods =  ~ intervention+0,
                               random = ~ as.factor(sr_no) | as.factor(study_ID), data = data_purchase3, method = "REML")
summary(meta_model5)

meta_model5_1 <-rma.mv(z_value, z_variance, mods =  ~ intervention, 
                               random = ~ as.factor(sr_no) | as.factor(study_ID), data = data_purchase3, method = "REML")
# random effects multi-level by intervention
# information, label, rebate significant positive
meta_model6 <-rma.mv(z_value, z_variance, mods = ~ appliance + 0,  
                               random = ~ as.factor(sr_no) | as.factor(study_ID), data = data_purchase3, method = "REML")
summary(meta_model6)

meta_model6_1 <-rma.mv(z_value, z_variance, mods =  ~ appliance, 
                               random = ~ as.factor(sr_no) | as.factor(study_ID), data = data_purchase3, method = "REML")
# random effects multi-level by appliance
# light, fridge, tv, washing machine significant positive


### INTERACTION INTERVENTION X APPLIANCE ###
data_purchase4 <- data_purchase3 %>%
  filter(appliance %in% c("Refrigerator", "Lighting", "Water Heater", "Air-Conditioner"))

meta_model7 <-rma.mv(z_value, z_variance, mods =  ~ intervention_category:appliance+0, 
                               random = ~ as.factor(sr_no) | as.factor(study_ID), data = data_purchase4, method = "REML")
# economic incentives x refrigerator have a negative sign  
summary(meta_model7)

# run a model with control variables included
#control_formula <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(controlvars, collapse = "+"), "+ 0"))
#meta_model8 <-rma.mv(z_value, z_variance, mods = control_formula,  
                               #random = ~ as.factor(sr_no) | as.factor(study_ID), data = data_purchase3, method = "REML")

# numeric and binary variables are causing errors

# effects don't change too much from inclusion of 'outliers'

# Train papers show weird results for loan and z_values
```

```{r}
### FOREST PLOT ### 

coef_summary5 <- coef(summary(meta_model5))
forest(coef_summary5$estimate, ci.lb = coef_summary5$ci.lb, ci.ub = coef_summary5$ci.ub, 
       slab = row.names(coef_summary5), showweights = F, atransf = F, shade="zebra",xlab = "z-value")

rownames(coef_summary5) <- c("Information \n(n = 68)","Label \n(n = 77)","Rebate \n(n = 31)","Subsidy \n(n = 27)")

coef_summary6 <- coef(summary(meta_model6))

rownames(coef_summary6) <- c("Air-Conditioner \n(n = 31)","Clothes Dryer \n(n = 6)","Dishwasher \n(n = 4)","Heat Pump \n(n = 18)","Lighting \n(n = 23)","Refrigerator \n(n = 54)","TV \n(n = 12)","Washing Machine \n(n = 13)","Water Heater \n(n = 43)")

forest(coef_summary6$estimate, ci.lb = coef_summary6$ci.lb, ci.ub = coef_summary6$ci.ub, 
       slab = row.names(coef_summary6), showweights = F, atransf = F, xlab = "z-value")

forest(coef_summary6$estimate, ci.lb = coef_summary6$ci.lb, ci.ub = coef_summary6$ci.ub,
       slab = row.names(coef_summary6), showweights = TRUE, atransf = F,  shade="zebra", xlab = "z-value")

### from bi ###
average_estimate5 <- mean(coef_summary5$estimate)
ggplot(coef_summary5,
       aes(x = row.names(coef_summary5), y = estimate)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = ci.lb, ymax = ci.ub),
                 size = 1.5, alpha = 1, colour = "red")  +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = average_estimate5, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", size = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = 3.5, y = average_estimate5 - 0.05, label = paste("Average:", round(average_estimate5, 2))) + 
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.15, 0.35)) +
  labs(x = "", y = "z-value") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 25))

average_estimate6 <- mean(coef_summary6$estimate)
ggplot(coef_summary6,
       aes(x = row.names(coef_summary6), y = estimate)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = ci.lb, ymax = ci.ub),
                 size = 1.5, alpha = 1, colour = "red")  + 
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = average_estimate6, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", size = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = 6, y = average_estimate6 - 0.05, label = paste("Average:", round(average_estimate6, 2))) + 
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.15, 0.35)) +
  labs(x = "", y = "z-value") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 25)) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust=1))
ggsave("appliances_forest.png", width = 12.5, height = 9.375)
```

```{r}
### PUBLICATION BIAS ASSESSMENT ###
library(lmtest)

### EGGERS TEST ### 

# Define a color palette with enough colors for each unique appliance
my_colors <- c("blue", "red", "green", "purple", "orange", "yellow", "pink", "brown", "gray")

### FUNNEL PLOT ###

funnel(
  data_purchase3$z_value, 
  v = data_purchase3$z_variance,
  ylim = c(0, 0.3),
  col = my_colors[as.factor(data_purchase3$appliance)], 
  legend = FALSE # We'll create the legend manually
)

# Create the legend manually using the legend() function
legend("topright", # Position of the legend
       legend = levels(as.factor(data_purchase3$appliance)), # Legend labels
       col = my_colors, # Legend colors
       pch = 15, # Point type (change if needed)
       title = "Appliance" # Legend title (change if needed)
)

funnel(
  data_purchase3$z_value, 
  v = data_purchase3$z_variance,
  ylim = c(0, 0.3),
  col = my_colors[as.factor(data_purchase3$intervention_category)],

)
```

```{r}
# identify outliers
# these thresholds are identified by looking at the graphs and identifying the peaks

threshold <- 0.1

x5 <- cooks.distance(meta_model5)
plot(x5, type="l", pch=19, xlab="Observed Outcome", ylab="Cook's Distance")
for (i in 1:length(x5)) {
  if (x5[i] > 0.1) {
    text(i, x5[i], i, cex = 1, pos = 4, col = "red")
  }
}
# 11, 130, 133, 134

below_threshold_rows5 <- which(x5 < threshold)
data_purchase5 <- data_purchase3[below_threshold_rows5,]
above_threshold_rows5 <- which(x5 > threshold)
outlier_cooksd5 <- data_purchase3[above_threshold_rows5,]

threshold6 <- 0.5

x6 <- cooks.distance(meta_model6)
plot(x6, type="l", pch=19, xlab="Observed Outcome", ylab="Cook's Distance")
for (i in 1:length(x6)) {
  if (x6[i] > threshold6) {
    text(i, x6[i], i, cex = 1, pos = 4, col = "red")
  }
}

below_threshold_rows6 <- which(x6 < threshold)
data_purchase6 <- data_purchase3[below_threshold_rows6,]
above_threshold_rows6 <- which(x6 > threshold)
outlier_cooksd6 <- data_purchase3[above_threshold_rows6,]
```

```{r}
res5 <- rma(z_value, z_variance, mods =  ~ intervention+0, 
                               random = ~ as.factor(sr_no) | as.factor(study_ID), data = data_purchase3, method = "REML")
# what is the difference between using rma and rma.mv

# explore influence diagnostics
sav5 <- influence(res5)
sav5

#cov.r
plot(sav5$inf$cov.r, type = "l", xlab = "index", ylab = "cov.r",
          xlim = c(1,203), ylim = c(0.25, 1.1))

# Adding labels for values less than 0.9
for (i in 1:length(sav5$inf$cov.r)) {
  if (sav5$inf$cov.r[i] < 0.9) {
    text(i, sav5$inf$cov.r[i], i, cex = 0.5, pos = 1, col = "red")
  }
}

# including effect sizes 133, 134, 167, 11, 188 and 194 reduces precision

# cook.d
plot(sav5$inf$cook.d, type = "l", xlab = "index", ylab = "cook.d",
          xlim = c(1,203), ylim = c(0, 1.5))

# Adding labels for values above 0.75
for (i in 1:length(sav5$inf$cook.d)) {
  if (sav5$inf$cook.d[i] > 0.75) {
    text(i, sav5$inf$cook.d[i], i, cex = 0.5, pos = 1, col = "red")
  }
}

# 133 and 134 are outliers again 

# Train & Atherton study - refrigerator & rebate 

# this seems like an important outlier and we should test for results without this outlier

# do we need to explain in the paper why outliers are like that?

res6 <- rma(z_value, z_variance, mods =  ~ appliance+0, 
                               random = ~ as.factor(sr_no) | as.factor(study_ID), data = data_purchase3, method = "REML")
# what is the difference between using rma and rma.mv

# explore influence diagnostics for appliance-specific model
sav6 <- influence(res6)
sav6

#cov.r
plot(sav6$inf$cov.r, type = "l", xlab = "index", ylab = "cov.r",
          xlim = c(1,203), ylim = c(0, 1.1))

# Adding labels for values less than 0.9
for (i in 1:length(sav6$inf$cov.r)) {
  if (sav6$inf$cov.r[i] < 0.9) {
    text(i, sav6$inf$cov.r[i], i, cex = 0.5, pos = 1, col = "red")
  }
}

# including effect sizes 133, 134, 167, 11, 188 and 194 reduces precision + 143 and 132, 135

# cook.d
plot(sav6$inf$cook.d, type = "l", xlab = "index", ylab = "cook.d",
          xlim = c(1,203), ylim = c(0, 1.5))

# Adding labels for values above 0.75
for (i in 1:length(sav6$inf$cook.d)) {
  if (sav6$inf$cook.d[i] > 0.75) {
    text(i, sav6$inf$cook.d[i], i, cex = 0.5, pos = 1, col = "red")
  }
}

# 133 and 134 again
```

```{r}
# create binary variables for all control factor variables

# iterate over each factor variable
for (var_name in controlvars) {
  
  # get unique factor levels
  
  levels <- unique(data_purchase3[[var_name]])
  
  # create binary variables for each factor level
  for (level in levels) {
    # create a new column name by appending the factor level to the variable name
    new_col_name <- paste(var_name, level, sep = "_")
    
    # create a binary variable for the current factor level
    data_purchase3[[new_col_name]] <- as.integer(data_purchase3[[var_name]] == level)
  }
}

```

```{r}
# create a list of control variables
data_purchase3$n_interventions <- as.factor(data_purchase3$n_interventions)
controlvars <- c( "counterfactual",
                  "n_interventions",
                 "intervention",
                 "appliance",
                 # "continent",
                 "OECD",
                 "statistical_technique",
                 "study_design",
                 "incentive_follow_through",
                 "experimental_setting",
                   # "participant_type",
                 "aware_of_study",
                 "opt_in",
                 "randomisation_dummy",
                 "outOfSampleBias",
                 "reportingBiases",
                 "controls_energy_prices",
                 "controls_environmental_attitudes",
                 "controls_demographics")

metregvar <- c("z_value", "z_variance")
dfbms <- data_purchase3 %>%  select(all_of(metregvar))
dfbms <- mutate_if(dfbms, is.character, as.numeric)
dfbms <- mutate_if(dfbms, is.logical, as.numeric)
```

```{r}
# BMA data preparation 
# create binary variables for all control factor variables

# iterate over each factor variable
for (var_name in controlvars) {
  
  # get unique factor levels
  
  levels <- unique(data_purchase3[[var_name]])
  
  # create binary variables for each factor level
  for (level in levels[-1]) {
    # create a new column name by appending the factor level to the variable name
    new_col_name <- paste(var_name, level, sep = "_")
    
    # create a binary variable for the current factor level
    dfbms[[new_col_name]] <- as.numeric(data_purchase3[[var_name]] == level)
  }
}
```
